test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Read the following statements and select the appropriate options:

**Statement 1:** A budget deficit is encountered when the total expenditure of the government is greater than its total revenue, excluding borrowings.

**Statement 2:** A budget deficit is faced when the total revenue of the government is greater than its expenditure in a fiscal year.

options.text: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct

solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement 1 is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** A budget deficit is encountered when the **total expenditure of the government exceeds its total revenue, excluding borrowings**. This definition aligns with the economic concept of a budget deficit. *Hence, Statement 1 is correct.*
 
• **Statement 2:** This statement incorrectly reverses the concept of a budget deficit. If the total revenue of the government is greater than its expenditure, it results in a budget surplus, not a deficit. *Hence, Statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• A **budget deficit** occurs when the government’s expenditure on services, infrastructure, and other public sector needs surpasses its revenue collections (excluding borrowing).
 
• A common source of revenue for governments includes **taxation, non-tax revenues, and dividends**, whereas expenditures include welfare programs, salaries, interest payments, and infrastructure spending.
 
• To cover a budget deficit, governments often rely on borrowing, which may take the form of issuing bonds or loans from domestic and international markets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Budget Deficits:**

 
 
• **Revenue Deficit:** It occurs when the government’s total revenue receipts are less than its revenue expenditures.
 
• **Fiscal Deficit:** This is the total borrowing requirement of the government. It is calculated as the difference between total expenditure and total receipts (excluding borrowings).
 
• **Primary Deficit:** This is the fiscal deficit excluding interest payments on previous borrowings. It reflects the current year's borrowing needs.
 
 
 
• **Impacts of a Budget Deficit:**
 
 
• Governments may resort to borrowing, leading to an increase in public debt.
 
• Excessive deficits can lead to inflation if financed by printing money.
 
• In the long term, persistent deficits may lead to economic instability.
 
 
 
• **Budget Surplus:** A budget surplus occurs when the government’s total revenue exceeds its total expenditure in a fiscal year. This allows governments to reduce debt or invest in infrastructure.
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• India often reports fiscal deficits in its Union Budget, reflecting the need for borrowing to fund development and welfare programs.
 
• Countries such as Germany and Switzerland have occasionally achieved budget surpluses due to high revenues and controlled expenditures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government Budget:** A government budget is an annual financial statement presenting its anticipated revenue and expenditure for the coming fiscal year.
 
• **Fiscal Responsibility:** Governments adopt fiscal responsibility laws, such as the **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003,** in India, to ensure fiscal discipline.
 
• **Balanced Budget:** In a balanced budget, government revenues are equal to expenditures. While rare, such budgets are considered fiscally ideal for long-term stability.
